hazards.hazard: Chlorosilane polymer deposits (several hundred kg) ignite spontaneously or react violently with wash water when channel covers are removed, causing fire/explosion and burn injuries
hazards.reason: Package states polymers 'known to be able to ignite'; history of burn injury during exchanger dismantling 3 years ago with corrective actions not followed up; hydrolysis step has no quantitative end-point, used only 11 kg water over 20 winter days for several hundred kg polymer; high-pressure water洗

hazards.hazard: Hydrogen generated by hydrolysis and trapped in polymer releases rapidly when polymer-laden wash water or exhaust contacts NaOH in scrubber/drainage, causing explosion
hazards.reason: Direct history: 2 years ago explosion in drainage tank when NaOH contacted residue from gas-gas exchanger dismantling; attributed to 'fast hydrogen release from polymer plus alkali' and 'judged not possible without alkali'; current procedure vents HX-B exhaust to NaOH scrubber during washing

hazards.hazard: Incomplete hydrolysis leaves reactive polymer that generates HCl, heat, and H2 when contacted by high-pressure wash water inside tubes
hazards.reason: Hydrolysis used humidified N2 (0.8 vol% H2O) at ambient winter temperature, only 09:00–17:00 for 20 days, total ~11 kg water for several hundred kg polymer; no temperature control; 9-day holiday interruption; no quantitative end-point criterion; chlorosilanes react with water

hazards.hazard: Residual HCl and chlorosilane vapors escape during channel cover removal despite nitrogen blanketing, exposing 18+ workers to toxic/corrosive gases
hazards.reason: Pre-treatment includes dry N2 blows but no verification of residual gas concentrations; N2 flow 20 Nm³/h at 0.018 MPa may be insufficient for HX-B volume (293 tubes × 4 m + covers); hazard levels not classified; training does not cover polymer hazards; many observers/trainees present

hazards.hazard: Runaway exothermic hydrolysis in confined tubes during high-pressure washing causes pressure burst, tube rupture, and projectile debris/chemical spray
hazards.reason: Polymers deposit on tube inner walls; washing with high-pressure water through open upper cover; no temperature or pressure monitoring during wash; confined tube geometry (ID 28.2 mm, 4 m long) can trap pressure; chlorosilanes react with water exothermically

hazards.hazard: Mechanical failure during handling of 4,800–6,300 kg exchanger and 300 kg channel covers by crane truck causes crush/impact injuries
hazards.reason: Package notes 'seized bolts delay opening' requiring pre-replacement; covers 'hung from crane truck'; washing area uses 'timber supports'; multiple contractor workers unfamiliar with equipment; no mention of lift plan or exclusion zone

hazards.hazard: Flammable/toxic emissions from HX-B washing drift to adjacent activated carbon unit or crude distillation pipe rack, triggering secondary fire/explosion
equipment: activated carbon adsorption unit (resin piping, slate wall, steel frame)
crude distillation column No. 2 pipe rack
hazards.reason: Washing area 'near the activated carbon unit and the No. 2 crude distillation pipe rack'; open area with only 'flame-retardant resin sheeting'; temporary floodlights present (ignition sources); neighboring companies in same complex

hazards.hazard: Fixed nitrogen purge parameters (20 Nm³/h, 0.018 MPa) are inadequate for actual polymer deposit volume, leaving flammable/toxic residues
hazards.reason: Purge parameters fixed in work standard but deposit mass 'estimated several hundred kg' in 293 tubes × 4 m; no verification step (O₂/LEL meter, gas analysis) mentioned; work standard has no quantitative end-points and is changeable within section

hazards.hazard: Organizational gaps (unclassified hazard levels, no polymer hazard training, unchecked work-standard changes, unfollowed corrective actions) allow unsafe deviations during abnormal conditions
hazards.reason: Package explicitly states: hazard levels of non-routine work not classified; training does not cover polymer hazards; work standards approved by section manager and may be changed within section; corrective actions from 3-year-old burn injury not followed up

hazards.hazard: Vinyl sheet covering lower channel opening fails during upper-cover tube washing, releasing water, debris, and gases onto workers
hazards.reason: Procedure: after lower cover removal and washing, 'cover the opening with vinyl sheet'; later upper cover opened and tubes washed with high-pressure water; vinyl sheet not rated for pressure, chemical, fire, or mechanical load; temporary measure in open area
